- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to avoid premature bottoming.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a steep drop; cap forecast decline to 3–4% below peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0 in 3 days), model often fails to adjust; delay forecast correction until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model tends to overpredict mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7), reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect slower reversion.
- When sentiment is negative and prices are near 30-day low, model often underestimates recovery; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to avoid missing rebound.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model may overfit recent trends; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
